content.comment_body: Hello, After successfully installing the software for [product_name] [version_no], I encounter an error when attempting to use most of the "Tools->Transfer" options. Additionally, I am unable to access the device through the application, as the transfer function does not work. Here are my system details:
Please refer to this topic, with particular focus on a post by [user_name]. Bug report: Java error in [product_name] [version_no] on Linux.
Thank you for your response. This resolved my problem. A specific command was necessary in my case.
Much appreciated. There is a workaround for Fedora/Red Hat distributions, based on instructions posted by [user_name]. The file to edit is [product_name]_[version_no]/lib/classes.jar.

The usual method suggested by [user_name] does not appear to work on Linux Mint 18 64-bit using [product_name] [version_no]. The error continues to occur, though the workaround does function correctly on a Raspberry Pi. Any suggestions are welcome! Kind regards, [user_name]

I managed to get [product_name] [version_no] working on Debian 9 (Stretch). While I normally use Debian 10 (Buster), I was unable to make it function there due to issues between [product_name] and JDK 11 (with JDK 8 unavailable in Buster). I had to run it on Stretch with JDK 8 under QEMU, which worked well enough. I am sharing this because I spent considerable time due to following advice that interface config files should be in /etc/sysconfig/netsuse/, but discovered from other posts that placing them in /etc/sysconfig/network/ finally solved the issue. It may depend on specific environments, so if one folder does not work, be sure to try the other.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering a Java exception related to 'adapter type is not supported' during transfer operations with [product_name] [version_no] on various Linux distributions. This problem blocks communication and data transfer to the device. The success of workarounds varies, influenced by OS types and Java versions. Solutions require manual adjustments, such as modifying system or network configuration files, resulting in time-consuming and unintuitive troubleshooting.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the application to work reliably after installation, particularly for standard device communication and transfer features, without needing extensive workarounds or technical troubleshooting.
